messages:
marco (support): FYI escalation from Acme — their Dedicated stack in a VPC is getting 401s only when routed through their ALB. Direct to the instance works. Repro steps below. :frowning_face:

john_acme (customer): repro: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://dedicated.acme.internal/generate 
> HTTP/2 302
> location: /oauth2/start?rd=...
followup curl to backend (after ALB) shows 401 and no Authorization header present.

marco (support): can you paste the raw request/response headers you see on the backend? curious if ALB is stripping or rewriting.

john_acme (customer): here's tcpdump from the backend host (redacted):
```
GET /generate HTTP/1.1
Host: dedicated.acme.internal
User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
Accept: */*
Cookie: alb-auth=...
X-Forwarded-For: 10.10.0.5
# NOTE: Authorization header absent here
```
They say they previously had a passthrough ALB, then enabled ALB's Authenticate (OIDC) action to offload SSO at the edge.

nina (eng): :eyes: ALB authenticate action will perform a redirect and set a cookie for the user session — it does not preserve the original Authorization header by design. If you flip on authenticate, ALB handles the auth handshake and doesn't forward the bearer header because ALB assumes it is OEM-managed. Did they expect the original bearer to still be forwarded?

john_acme (customer): we expected the internal service to still receive the bearer because the token is per-service. Our gateway validates it and applies per-tenant routing. ALB docs said it would inject x-amzn-oidc-data headers, but we saw none.

aubrey (sre): Quick checklist: 1) confirm ALB action type (authenticate vs forward) 2) check target group protocol (HTTP vs HTTPS) 3) look for X-Amzn-Oidc-* headers on backend 4) ensure any Istio envoy filters aren't normalizing/stripping headers. I can grab proxy logs if you want.

john_acme (customer): ALB listener rule shows "authenticate-oidc" then "forward" to target group. Target group is HTTP on port 8080. No X-Amzn-Oidc-* in backend requests.

eli (eng-infra): If ALB completed the OIDC exchange it'll set a session cookie (ALB does this) and will not forward the incoming Authorization header. The cookie name is usually AWSELBAuth or alb-auth (config dependent). The ALB also adds headers like x-amzn-oidc-accesstoken if it has the token, but only after the OIDC flow; in some setups ALB intentionally removes Authorization to avoid leaking credentials to backend. This is expected behavior for ALB authenticate flow.

marco (support): So root cause likely the ALB authenticate action interfering with header pass-through. Two paths to resolution: a) terminate auth at ALB and update our gateway to consume alb cookie / x-amzn-oidc-* headers instead of Authorization; or b) switch to a passthrough LB (NLB) or remove authenticate action and perform auth in Istio/ext_authz on the Dedicated gateway. Which is the customer's preference?

john_acme (customer): we prefer option (b) — keep our gateway validating the bearer. We thought ALB would be a transparent L7 proxy. Any immediate workarounds?

nina (eng): Workaround: change ALB listener rule to forward to a different TargetGroup that doesn't have authenticate action OR move auth to Istio (recommended). If you must keep ALB authenticate for web UI, you can make a separate ALB path for API traffic that forwards (no authenticate) to the same backend cluster.

aubrey (sre): Also watch cookie SameSite and Secure flags — ALB cookie is for browser sessions; API bearer tokens in Authorization are unrelated. Don't mix the two. If your traffic is non-browser (machine-to-machine) use a forward-only ALB or NLB TLS passthrough.

john_acme (customer): thanks — we changed the API listener to a pure forward rule to target-group-api (no authenticate) and now backend sees Authorization header again. Tests look good: HTTP 200 returned and gateway validates token. :white_check_mark:

eli (eng-infra): Added note for docs: call out ALB authenticate behavior in Dedicated onboarding guide — many customers assume passthrough. I'll open a PR to the private deployment checklist. ops-bot: created issue GOV-401 in infra docs.

ops-bot: Issue GOV-401 created: "ALB authenticate: note about header stripping and recommended NLB/passthrough patterns for API traffic".

marco (support): Closing loop with customer — please ping if you see any anomalies. Also leaving recommended config summary: use separate listener/rule for browser SSO (authenticate) and API traffic (forward) or terminate TLS at gateway and use NLB for pure passthrough.

john_acme (customer): verified. Appreciate the quick turnaround, team.

nina (eng): adding a snippet for customers encountering this: 
```
# ALB rule: browser UI -> authenticate-oidc -> forward -> targets (UI-TG)
# API rule: /api/* -> forward -> targets (API-TG)  # NO authenticate
```
This avoids ALB removing Authorization for API calls.

marco (support): tagging docs for follow-up. :thumbsup:
